dedupe_keys.name: 5g today field trial of 5g broadcast in bavaria 2017 to 2019

description: This testbed case covers 5G TODAY, a research project that tested the broadcast of television over mobile network standards from high towers in southern Bavaria. The partners were the public broadcaster Bayerischer Rundfunk, the broadcast research institute IRT, the antenna maker Kathrein, the transmitter maker Rohde & Schwarz and the operator Telefonica Germany, with funding from the Bavarian Research Foundation from 2017. Two high-power transmitters, at Ismaning near Munich and on the Wendelstein mountain, each radiated 100 kW effective power in the FeMBMS mode (Further evolved Multimedia Broadcast Multicast Service) of the 3GPP standards, testing coverage of cells with a radius of up to 60 km, far larger than normal mobile cells. In 2019 the partners reported good mobile TV reception across large parts of the measured area and said the results would feed standardisation of 5G broadcast. Coverage: an area of Upper Bavaria around Munich, 2017 to 2019. Format and access: press releases and trade press, free; project pages at IRT are no longer online since the institute closed. Caveats: detailed measurement data were not found; the trial tested a broadcast mode, not network resilience. Simulation uses: design of high-power, high-tower broadcast networks that can carry TV and alerts to phones, and coverage modelling. Related records: the Ofcom broadcast transmitter parameters and the Canadian broadcasting database give real transmitter data for coverage studies.
